ds: Illicit supply and diversion of firearms, ammunition and components, including straw purchases, illegal manufacturing, end-user certificate fraud and brokering outside licence. Financial indicators arise in dealer payments, shipping, brokers and cash purchases.

src.t: UN Protocol against the Illicit Manufacturing of and Trafficking in Firearms (2001)
UNODC, Global Study on Firearms Trafficking 2020 (2020)
SIPRI, Trends in International Arms Transfers (annual fact sheet)

rat: Dealer and broker payments, trade documentation and shipping for transfers, plus cash and straw purchases by individuals; arms dealers are regulated non-bank businesses.

ind.n: Multiple firearm or component purchases by one person for others
ind.cx: Repeated purchases of guns, parts or ammunition inconsistent with sport use, paid by different people.
ind.fp: Collectors and ranges buy in volume.
ind.ds: Repeated purchases of guns, parts or ammunition inconsistent with sport use, paid by different people.

ind.n: Brokers or dealers lacking licences or end-user certificates
ind.cx: Intermediary arranges transfers without export licences.
ind.ds: Intermediary arranges transfers without export licences.

ind.n: Shipping through high-risk transit hubs with changed destinations
ind.cx: Arms shipments change consignee or route.
ind.ds: Arms shipments change consignee or route.

ind.n: Purchase of 3D-printing, CNC machines and parts for gun manufacture
ind.cx: Orders for firearm blueprint files, receivers, jigs.
ind.ds: Orders for firearm blueprint files, receivers, jigs.

ind.n: Payments from or to sanctioned or embargoed parties
ind.cx: Counterparties on arms embargo or sanctions lists.
ind.ds: Counterparties on arms embargo or sanctions lists.

ind.n: Cash purchases with prompt resale or export
ind.cx: Weapons purchased for cash and quickly moved abroad.
ind.ds: Weapons purchased for cash and quickly moved abroad.

ind.n: Armed groups or militias as end users linked to customers
ind.cx: Customer's counterparties are tied to armed groups.
ind.ds: Customer's counterparties are tied to armed groups.

ind.n: Fake commercial front using civilian goods descriptions
ind.cx: Containers described as machinery or toys with weights conflicting with documents.
ind.ds: Containers described as machinery or toys with weights conflicting with documents.

ctl.ds: Participates in sector, regulator and public-private forums and platform cooperation to receive and share typologies and indicators where lawful. It keeps scenarios current.

Translates published and sanitised typologies and red flags into targeted monitoring scenarios and context-aware rules that are reviewed periodically. It aligns monitoring with known criminal methods.

Requires end-user statements, authenticates their signatories, verifies licences and sites, and obtains post-delivery reports for goods and funds. It confirms that goods or funds reach the stated end use.

Verifies licences, registrations and supervisory status of customers, agents and counterparties against regulator registers before onboarding and periodically. It confirms legal authority to operate and detects unlicensed activity.

Blocks or refers transfers, goods, services and system access linked to embargoed or comprehensively sanctioned territories using address, route, payment-country and device-location signals. It prevents prohibited dealings from being processed.

Compares shipping routes, ports and delivery points with typical lanes and risk lists, and requests explanation for unusual hubs or indirect delivery. It reveals diversion, transshipment and evasion routing.

ctl.n: Lifestyle and high-value purchase consistency review
ctl.ds: Compares observed spending, luxury and asset purchases and personal-type use of business funds with documented income and wealth during periodic reviews and alerts. It highlights unexplained affluence that may indicate illicit income.

Screens customers, owners, counterparties, vessels, dealers and addresses against sanctions, enforcement and restricted-party lists at onboarding and ongoing, using fuzzy matching and secondary identifiers. Potential matches are held for adjudication before service or funds are released.
Reconciles cash, stock purchases, sales and exports with declared business activity to test whether deposits are plausible. It is used to identify unrecorded or injected cash.

Applies targeted enhanced checks to customer types or sectors known to be vulnerable to misuse, such as cash-intensive trades, money service businesses, high-value dealers, professional services, charities or waste handlers. Questions and evidence are tailored to how the sector normally operates.

Runs continuous screening of customers, owners, introducers, suppliers and counterparties against curated news, leaks, regulatory notices and enforcement releases, with reliability grading and identity disambiguation. It surfaces negative information that registers and lists do not carry.

Routes potential sanctions, proscription or restricted-party exposure to a specialist sanctions or legal team for decision before proceeding, and sets conditions for finance and insurance. It ensures complex legal judgements are made by qualified people.
Tailors training content and frequency to role and risk for finance, relationship, underwriting and compliance staff, with feedback of quality assurance findings. It builds baseline competence.

ctl.n: Trade document review and consistency checking
ctl.ds: Trained staff and automated checks review goods, parties, routes, descriptions and codes across invoice, bill of lading and payment documents. It exposes mismatches and falsified paper.
